detailZh: 也许部分是因为马德里马德里赛道赛道带来的诸多悬念，车手们在抵达这座西班牙首都时状态极佳，并在马德里首个“行动日”有很多话题可以讨论。
无论是法拉利在蒙扎噩梦之后的余波、赛道本身、某支车队的资源问题显现、驾驶风格分析，还是2026年F1最新成员的学习情况，都有很多值得深入探讨的内容。开始上课吧。
法拉利车手称隔阂已经消除
正如F1的常态一样，法拉利车手刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔周四在马德里尽力淡化围绕蒙扎艰难周末之后的种种传闻。
汉密尔顿表示，赛后他们进行了一次富有成效的面对面交谈，在谈话中他们“消除”了对于首圈那次纠缠的任何意见分歧。
勒克莱尔表示，现在“非常清楚我们接下来应该做什么，或者应该避免什么”。
汉密尔顿赛后与车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔的交谈中，也没有提到交往规则的问题。
所以法拉利一切都好，对吧？其实，只有当他们再次在赛道上相遇时，我们才能知道答案。
重要的是，汉密尔顿在蒙扎之后所要求的所有改变，无法像马德里那样迅速落实。他形容这是一个“更长期的过程”。
“这里有大量相互关联的部分。有很多人。有一种存在了很久很久的文化。要挪动这些大块的东西并不容易。”
他认为法拉利在执行和运营方面“最终会达到我们需要的水准”，但肯定不会是在马德里的这个周末。——乔什·萨蒂尔
勒克莱尔在周日下午从医疗中心获释后表示，他还需要接受“相当多的额外检查”，以确认自己是否“完全无碍”能够参加马德里的比赛。
撞车后他立即透露“右眼看东西视野不太好”，不过那很快就恢复了。
周四在马德里，当被问及蒙扎之后检查了哪些项目时，勒克莱尔说：“查了相当多的东西。但那是一次挺严重的撞车。从外面看可能也挺严重的，而且我自己感觉也很严重。
“有时候从事故外面看很大，但在车里其实没什么。但下车的时候，我感觉不太舒服。
不过其实那只是惊吓造成的。头几天我做了很多检查，也接受了很多治疗，主要是针对颈部，因为我感觉有点发紧，我想这很正常。
“但现在我很好，我做的所有检查都没问题。”——原音译保留
无论是正式来到F1的赛场，在模拟器上体验，还是如今亲身到场，马德里环（马德里赛道）赛道都印证了人们最初听到F3测试中出现19次红旗时的那种震惊。
乔治·拉塞尔说，当他第一次听到这个数字时，他很惊讶它竟然这么高——而等他完成模拟器测试后，他又惊讶它居然没有更高。
这条被称为“疯狂”和“可怕”、并且是赛历上最“复杂”的马德里环赛道，被认为有望带来一个类似摩纳哥的、节奏逐步提升（并不断被红旗打断）的比赛周末——但它在调校方面不像摩纳哥那种“没有直道、没有高速弯”的赛道那么直观，所以这也将是一个令人头疼的问题。
但这一切的关键在于排位赛。奥利·比尔曼和亚历克斯·阿尔本指出，最好的超车机会受阻于倾斜的弯角入弯方式，这意味着超车需要在刹车区之前完成，而不是在刹车过程中完成——如果真有超车机会的话。
但这22位车手得先把赛车完好无损地带到发车区，然后才轮得到操心这些。——瓦连京·霍罗恩日伊
在赛车运动中，几乎没有比冠军领跑者滔滔不绝地说'你们懂的，我根本不看积分榜，我只专注一场一场比赛'更让人疲惫的事了。这种话几乎总是浪费口舌，说出来纯属白费。
安东内利目前是少数的例外之一——因为正如他所言，'我认为蒙扎就是证明，说明我没有在想冠军的事，也没有为此担忧'。
这个“证明”既体现在他比赛初期的猛烈追赶中，也体现在与梅赛德斯队友拉塞尔缠斗时差点在主直道变弯（Variante del Rettifilo）的砂石区毁掉一切的那次经历中。这种激进的驾驶方式本可能让安东内利当众出丑，但反而把他的积分领先优势扩大到了60分以上——而且他誓言暂时不会放弃这种风格。
“当然，将来可能会有某些场合，在做出某个决定之前，我会考虑到总冠军——但我想要避免的，是带着对总冠军的思考或担忧去参加自由练习、排位赛，甚至是一场比赛。”
“这就是我无论如何都要避免的事情。”
角田裕毅指出被忽视的2026年挑战
这一代一级方程式赛车受到了不少主力车手的批评，但那些在赛季中途才加入的车手又是怎么看的呢？
角田裕毅对2026年赛车的全新视角，揭示了一个被忽视的挑战，这是这一代“能量匮乏”的赛车所特有的。
在马德里，在他本赛季第三次代替出场之前，角田表示在出场圈（出场圈，指出维修站后的那一圈）上的能量管理是一个难题。
他说他必须提醒自己在出场圈上不要消耗太多能量，但前提是“如果你不使用能量，轮胎就会变冷，所以有时候你不得不更激进一些……”
“你想以100%的电量开始一圈。要牺牲位置，决定在哪里这么做，在哪里不要这么做。这非常复杂，而我在排位赛里把这件事搞砸了很多次。后果非常严重，”他加重语气说道。
“我低估了如果你没有把每件事都做对，会付出的代价或受到的惩罚有多大，而我在排位赛中确实亲身经历了这一点。”
不过，角田裕毅并没有对2026年的F1赛车提出严厉批评。
他补充说：“它更难了一些，而且要处理的事情多得多，[甚至]在出场圈如何进行开关模式的切换也是。所以，压力可能会更大。”
“但同时，在正赛中你可以有更多的超车。到目前为止，这是一辆我能很快适应的车，而且能很快跟上节奏。所以，我并不讨厌它。”
他仍在为2027年寻找席位，周四在西班牙，他表示自己“不想”继续留在场边。- 萨马特·卡纳尔
本赛季早些时候，刘易斯·汉密尔顿决定放弃使用模拟器来确立赛车调校的做法引发了很多讨论。
奥利·比尔曼认为，在模拟器工作量之少这方面，他和哈斯队友埃斯特班·奥孔是仅有的两名接近汉密尔顿水平的车手。
detailEn: Perhaps in part down to the abundance of intrigue about the Madring track, the drivers have arrived in the Spanish capital in great form and had plenty to discuss on the first day of 'action' in Madrid.

Whether it's the fallout from Ferrari's Monza nightmare, the track itself, one team's resource issue manifesting, driving style analysis or how F1 2026's newest classmate is learning, there's plenty to get into. Let's get started, class.
Ferrari drivers claim the air has been cleared
As has become the norm in F1, Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc did their best to diffuse any noise around the fallout from a bruising Monza weekend on Thursday in Madrid.
Hamilton said they had a productive face-to-face talk after the race, in which they “squashed” any differences of opinion over their opening lap run-in.
Leclerc said it’s now “very clear what we should do or avoid going forward”.
Rules of engagement didn’t come up in Hamilton’s post-race talks with team boss Fred Vasseur either.
So all is fine at Ferrari, right? Well, we’ll only know that when they meet again on track.
And importantly, all the changes Hamilton called for after Monza can’t be implemented as quickly as Madrid. He described it as “a longer-term process.
“There's a huge amount of moving parts. There's a lot of people. There's a culture that's been there for a long, long time. Moving big pieces is not so easy.”
He thinks Ferrari will “eventually get to the point we need” in terms of execution and operations, but it certainly won’t be this weekend in Madrid. - Josh Suttill
Having been released from the medical centre on Sunday afternoon after the crash, Leclerc said he would have “quite a few additional checks” to know if he’d be “fully fine” to race in Madrid.
He’d revealed his “right eye was not showing me great vision” immediately after the crash, though that cleared up soon afterwards.

On Thursday in Madrid, when asked what was checked after Monza, Leclerc said: “Quite a lot of things. But it was quite a big one. Probably from outside, it looked like a big one as well. But it felt also like a big one.
“Sometimes you can look quite big from outside, but from the car, it's fine. But going out, I wasn't feeling so well.
"But actually, it was just the shock. I did quite a lot of checks and quite a lot of treatments in the first few days, mostly for the neck, because I felt a little bit tight, which I guess is normal.
“But now I'm fine, all the checks I did were fine.” - JS
To the F1 grid, on the sim and now in the flesh, the Madring circuit has lived up to that initial shock of hearing about the 19 red flags in F3 testing.
George Russell said he was surprised by how high that number was when he first heard it - then surprised it hadn't been higher once he did his sim sessions.

Described as "crazy" and "scary" and the calendar's most "complicated", the Madring is being tipped for a Monaco-esque weekend of gradual pace and track ramp-up (and being peppered with red flags) - but it is less intuitive set-up-wise than the 'no straights, no high-speed corners' Monaco, so that will be a headache, too.

But it is all about qualifying. Ollie Bearman and Alex Albon pointed out that the best overtaking opportunities are hindered by angled corner entry meaning that overtakes will need to happen before the braking zone rather than on the brakes, if they happen at all.
But the 22 drivers need to get their cars to the grid in one piece before they can worry about any of that. - Valentin Khorounzhiy

There are few things more exhausting in motor racing than runaway championship leaders talking about how 'you guys, I don't look at the standings at all, I take it one race at a time'. That talk is almost always a waste of the molecular vibration required for it to be heard.
Antonelli right now is one of the rare exceptions - because, as he argued, "I think Monza was the proof that I wasn't thinking about or worrying about the championship".

That 'proof' is in both his charge early on and in nearly throwing it all away in the Variante del Rettifilo gravel while battling Mercedes team-mate George Russell. The aggression risked egg on Antonelli's face but instead pushed his points lead above 60 - and he vows not to abandon it just yet.

"Of course, there might be occasions in the future where, before taking a certain decision, I might think about the championship - but the thing I want to avoid is going to the track for a free practice or a qualifying, or even a race, thinking about or worrying about the championship.
"That's the thing I want to avoid, at all costs."
Tsunoda highlights overlooked 2026 challenge
This generation of Formula 1 cars has garnered plenty of criticism from mainstay drivers, but what about the driver who’s jumped in partway through the season?
Yuki Tsunoda’s fresh perspective on the 2026 cars has outlined an overlooked challenge unique to this energy-starved generation.
In Madrid, before his third substitute appearance of the season, Tsunoda said energy management on outlaps was a challenge.
He said he has to remind himself not to use too much energy during outlaps, the caveat being that “if you don't use the energy, the tyre is going to be cold, so you want to be sometimes aggressive…”

“You want to start the lap with 100% battery. Sacrifice places, where to do it, where to not. It was very complicated and something that I f****** up quite a lot in qualifying. The consequences were huge,” he said with emphasis.
“I was underestimating the amount of damage or penalty you'll get if you don't do everything right and I definitely experienced it in qualifying.”
Tsunoda wasn’t scathing about the F1 2026 cars, however.
He added: “It's a bit more difficult and there's a lot more things going on, [even] how to do the switch changes out lap. So, it can be more stressful.
“But at the same time, in the race you can have more overtakes. So far, it's a car that I'm able to adapt pretty quickly for me and able to be on the pace pretty quickly. So, I don’t hate it.”
He's still seeking a seat for 2027 and, on Thursday in Spain, he said he “doesn’t want to” remain on the sidelines. - Samarth Kanal
Much was made earlier this season about Lewis Hamilton's decision to ditch the simulator as a tool to establish set-up on his Ferrari.
Ollie Bearman reckons he and Haas team-mate Esteban Ocon are the only drivers even close to Hamilton in terms of how little sim work they do.

梅赛德斯车手基米·安东内利和乔治·拉塞尔讨论他们赢得2026年车手总冠军的希望。
乔治·拉塞尔坚称，他对基米·安东内利的节奏“确实有答案”，但承认要想在车手积分榜上追上这位梅赛德斯队友，还需要一些好运。
在上周末的意大利大奖赛上，拉塞尔本就渺茫的争冠希望遭受了打击：尽管20岁的安东内利因超出引擎部件配额被罚，从第19位发车，却依然击败他夺冠。
这一结果让在蒙扎从第二位发车的拉塞尔在还剩10站（从本周末马德里西班牙大奖赛开始）的情况下，落后安东内利66分。

拉塞尔赛季初是明显的夺冠热门，但至今只赢下两场大奖赛，而安东内利已赢七场，这位意大利车手一直更快，尤其是在比赛节奏方面。
当被问及是否处于对安东内利速度没有答案的境地时，拉塞尔回答说：“我确实有答案，我正在努力，而且已经大有改善。”
观看安东内利如何从第19位逆转至第一，在意大利大奖赛上取得惊人胜利。
“我对自己的这种进步非常满意，因为从根本上改变驾驶风格对很多车手来说是可以做到的，但真正用这种风格跑得快则是另一回事。”
在F1夏休前跌入低谷后，拉塞尔在荷兰和意大利交出了稳健的周末表现，但在周日仍无法击败安东内利。
“我觉得自夏休以来我的表现……我在三场排位赛中都排在他前面，在这两场比赛中我的比赛节奏也与他相当。而在休赛前我做不到这一点。我对这种进步绝对非常满意。”
“我们得看看赛季剩余时间会把我们带向何方。”
拉塞尔多次坚称，他的重点是提升自己的表现，而不是想着追赶安东内利，但在F1重返马德里之前，他承认如果今年要赢得自己的首个车手总冠军，运气将是必需的。
除了积分劣势，拉塞尔还必须在赛季结束前因使用新引擎部件而接受发车位处罚，这将使他在某场比赛中从队尾发车。
安东内利和拉塞尔在意大利大奖赛领先位置上轮对轮较量，展开多次史诗般的队友对决。
谈到自己夺冠的前景，拉塞尔说：“我不想自欺欺人。现实是，我的队友今年做得比我好。”
“我遇到了一些坏运气，但他配得上领先，现在他配得上他所处的位置。”
“从我这边来说，我只是一场一场地跑。我会努力赢下尽可能多的比赛。”
“如果我想赢得这个总冠军，我需要一些运气，这就是我们目前的处境。我对我们所处的位置相当现实。”
安东内利：我想避免去想总冠军
在对手们本被期望缩小差距的这个周末，安东内利取得胜利，进一步巩固了他作为夺冠绝对热门的地位。
在拉塞尔身后，法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿落后安东内利76分，而迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯以96分之差位列第四。
尽管位置稳固，安东内利声称现在考虑总冠军“还为时过早”。
安东内利：在“冲过最后终点线”之前，总冠军都不算赢下。
他说：“我甚至不知道还剩多少场比赛。十场？所以，还有很长的路要走。现在还早。”
“而且我真的不想在驾驶时想着总冠军。蒙扎就是证明，我当时驾驶时并没有想着或担心总冠军。”
“我只是为了赢而驾驶；为了做到最好，这就是心态。”
“当然，未来可能会有一些时候，在做出某个决定之前，我可能会考虑总冠军。”
“但我想避免的是，在进入一节自由练习或排位赛——甚至正赛——时想着或担心总冠军。这是我想不惜一切代价避免的事情。”

Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell discuss their hopes of winning the 2026 Drivers' Championship
George Russell insists he does "have an answer" to Kimi Antonelli's pace but admits he will need good fortune to catch his Mercedes team-mate at the top of the Drivers' Championship.

​​​​​​Russell suffered a demoralising blow to his already faint title hopes at last weekend's Italian Grand Prix when he was beaten to victory by Antonelli despite the 20-year-old having started from 19th on the grid after receiving a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.
The result saw Russell, who had started second in Monza, fall 66 points behind Antonelli with 10 rounds remaining, starting with this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.

Russell started the season as the clear title favourite but has won just two grands prix compared to Antonelli's seven, with the Italian being consistently quicker, especially in terms of race pace.
Asked about finding himself in situation where he doesn't have an answer to Antonelli's speed, Russell replied: "I do have an answer and I'm working on it, and it's been much improved.
Watch how Antonelli converted 19th to first to take a sensational victory at the Italian Grand Prix
"I'm very pleased with that sort of step I've taken because fundamentally changing the driving style is achievable for a lot of drivers, but then actually being fast with it is another topic."
Having reached a low point ahead of F1's summer break, Russell delivered solid weekends in the Netherlands and Italy, but was still unable to beat Antonelli on a Sunday.

"I feel my performance since the summer break has been... I've qualified ahead of him in the three qualifying sessions and my race pace has been on a par with him in these two races. And I couldn't say that pre-break. I'm definitely very pleased with that progression.
"We'll have to see where the rest of the season takes us."

Russell has repeatedly insisted his focus is on improving his own performances rather than thinking about catching Antonelli, but ahead of F1's return to Madrid he admitted luck will be required if he is to claim his maiden drivers' title this year.

In addition to his deficit, Russell will also have to take a grid penalty for taking new engine parts between now and the end of the season, which will see him start a race from the back of the field.
Antonelli and Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix lead in several epic team-mate battles
On his prospects of winning the title, Russell said: "I'm not trying to be delusional. The reality is my team-mate's done a better job than me this year.
"I've had some bad luck but he deserves to be leading and right now he deserves to be in the position he is.
"From my side, I'm just going race by race. I'm going to try and win as many as possible.
"If I want to win this championship, I'm going to need some luck and that's where we are. I'm sort of being quite realistic about the position we're in."
Antonelli: I want to avoid thinking about the championship
Antonelli's victory on a weekend where his rivals were expected to make ground on him has further cemented his status as an overwhelming favourite to close out the championship.
Behind Russell, Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton dropped 76 points behind Antonelli, while McLaren's Lando Norris trails by 96 points in fourth.
Despite the strength of his position, Antonelli claims it's "still early" to be thinking about the championship.
Antonelli: Championship not won until 'you cross final finish line'
He said: "I don't even know how many races are left. Ten? So, it's still a long way to go. It's still early.
"And I don't really want to drive thinking about championship. Monza was the proof that I wasn't driving thinking about or worrying about championship.
"I was just driving to win; to do my best and so that's the mindset.
"Of course, there might be occasions in the future where before taking a certain decision, I might think about the championship.

"But the thing I want to avoid is going on track for a free practice or a qualifying - or even a race - thinking about or worrying about the championship. That's the thing I want to avoid at all costs."

“但还有一些弯道相当像巴库，你从高速进入一个低速刹车区，边刹车边转向，所以很容易锁死轮胎。而一旦锁死，你就会直接撞上护墙。”
汉密尔顿补充道：“这些路肩可能与蒙特利尔那样的地方有些相似，显然梅赛德斯在那里速度很快，但那里的直道也要多得多。”
“这是一条极具挑战性的赛道。在我去过的所有新赛道中，这一条，也许还有沙特，是两条在掌握赛车状态和找到正确线路等方面难度最接近的赛道。”

"Of course, Jeddah is faster on average with the corners, but the walls are quite similar in how they are positioned.

"It's going to be tough. I think when F3 were testing here there were a lot of shunts, so it's not an easy track, easy to make a mistake also with the layout of the track. The kerbs that are there, we need to run over a few of them, and that's normally not the strong point of our car, but we will try to do the best we can."

Last month, a two-day Formula 3 test took place at the Madring and there were 19 red flags, mostly for crashes at several areas of the track.
Williams' Carlos Sainz, who has given some input into the circuit design, says the track is "different to what we're used to".

"It looks that the track has character, that it's charismatic, with a lot of different kinds of corners."

Qualifying is expected to be pivotal due to the difficulty of overtaking as most corners only have one racing line, so the drivers will be keen to push the limits come Saturday afternoon, even if it means taking huge risks.
Last week's shock pole-sitter Pierre Gasly believes it will create "huge adrenaline" for the drivers.
"The track layout is something I've never seen before. You have these crazy corners, blind corners, a huge banking," said the Alpine driver.

"It took me a few laps in the sim to get my head around what's where. It's very challenging because everything is twisty. I'm excited. I expect a really hectic weekend with lots of disruption and mistakes and we will have to make sure we are on the right side of it."
It will be particularly important for the championship contenders to keep out of the barriers so they don't lose big points to their rivals.

"It's a crazy circuit. I would put it as arguably the most risky circuit of the whole calendar because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque. The walls are very close, so there's no margin for error," said Russell.

"But then you have other corners that are quite like Baku, where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone, you're braking and turning at the same time, so locking tyres is going to be easy. And if you lock up, you'll be straight in the wall."

Hamilton added: "There's probably some similarities with these kerbs compared to somewhere like Montreal where you saw obviously Mercedes was very quick, but there was a lot more straights there as well.

"It's a massively challenging circuit. Of all the new tracks that I've gone to, this one, maybe Saudi, are the two closest in terms of how difficult it was to get on top of the car and find the right lines etc."

detailZh: 为什么马克斯·维斯塔潘不相信红牛在马德里会有惊人表现的说法
无论马德里赛道（马德里赛道）是否是一条考验车手技术的赛道，维斯塔潘都认为他无法仅凭一己之力制造惊喜、赢得胜利
当马克斯·维斯塔潘在蒙扎接受荷兰媒体采访时被问到，他现在是否认为自己本赛季在一级方程式中可能一场比赛都赢不了——这将是自他2015年首秀赛季以来的第一次——他给出了一个意味深长的回答：
“我显然绝不会把这种话说出口！”
然而去年，维斯塔潘确实说了这番话，而且似乎起了作用。在发表那一声明之后，这位红牛车手在赛季下半程的每一场大奖赛中都登上了领奖台，距离连续第五个世界冠军仅差两分。
不过，维斯塔潘比任何人都清楚，今年的情况完全不同，实现逆转几乎是不可能的。因此，十多年来首次经历一个整赛季没有分站冠军，是一个现实的可能。
“每次坐进赛车里，我总是追求最大化。如果有获胜的机会，我当然会全力以赴。但就目前的情况来看，这个机会并不大。”
一条全新的赛道带来了额外的问号，而人们的目光很快转向那些能够快速适应并获得竞争优势的杰出车手，例如维斯塔潘、阿隆索和刘易斯·汉密尔顿。
然而，维斯塔潘怀疑自己是否能在马德里的IFEMA园区周边的赛道上创造什么特别的表现，尽管这条赛道被描述为一条车手能比在蒙扎那样的赛道发挥更大作用的赛道。
“我的意思是，你可以把故事说得多么美好都行，对吧？不管是车手赛道还是不是，归根结底在一级方程式里你仍然需要一辆够快的赛车。”
这不仅适用于马德里环形赛道（马德里赛道），也适用于维斯塔潘的整个赛季。这位荷兰车手认为自己的表现处于很高的水平，但这并没有体现在比赛成绩中。
“作为一名车手，我今年感觉状态很好，但我没有赢下比赛。这是否意味着我是个糟糕的车手或者不够快？我不这么认为。”
“并不是说突然之间，因为这是一条比蒙扎或其他赛道更考验车手的赛道，你就能表现得好很多。”
维斯塔潘目前正在认真考虑这样一种情形：今年他可能一场比赛都赢不了
在马德里林赛道迎来首场大奖赛之前，大部分讨论都集中在这条赛道的危险性上。三级方程式测试期间出现了多达19次红旗，而威廉姆斯车队领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯则将这条F1赛历上的最新赛道形容为“赛车杀手”。
当被Motorsport.com问到马德里林赛道是否真的那么危险时，维斯塔潘回答：
“嗯，有可能是这样。在某些地方，只要你出现一点点失误，就可能酿成撞车。不过我的意思是，吉达也是一样的，这一点我们之前已经聊过了。”
“你只能去应对它，努力弄清楚极限在哪里，尽量把局面控制住。但当然，当你处在极限边缘时，犯一点小错误是很容易的。”
维斯塔潘提到吉达是有原因的。在他看来，那条赛道是与马德里赛道（马德里新赛道）最接近的类比，因为那里同样是一条街道赛道，任何失误都会受到严惩。
“就我的感受而言，是的。当然，这里的低速弯要多不少，但我得到的整体感觉确实有点像那条赛道，是的。”
维斯塔潘和劳森都把马德里赛道与吉达的街道赛道相提并论
红牛的替补车手兼临时队友利亚姆·劳森也认同这一比较，尤其是因为这两条赛道的共同特点是有很多盲弯。
“这些街道赛道的建造方式是这样的，护墙就沿着赛道的走向延伸，所以很多地方都非常看不到前方”，这位新西兰车手周四表示。
“有很多较快的连贯弯角，弯后面藏着东西，你根本看不见。吉达显然比这里更多这种情况，但我觉得在那方面有点相似。”
马德林赛道的许多路段都可能让车手吃亏，但由5号弯和6号弯组成的减速弯看起来肯定是其中最具挑战性的路段之一。
“如果你压到第一块路缘石太多，它会把你弹到第二块路缘石上，然后又把你弹向护墙。想要在这样的路段保持精准其实相当困难。”劳森承认道。
“我看过很多视频，F3赛车把两块路缘石都狠狠压上去，有的安然无恙，有的则没能幸免，所以这绝对是赛道上一个棘手的路段。刹车区显然也不是直的，所以既要避免抱死又要全力推迟刹车点，将会相当艰难。”
最后，劳森认为车手们在马德里将无法完全压榨到极限，否则就会感受到2026年动力单元的性能局限。
“不像摩纳哥那样，不是的。我认为摩纳哥是我们可以全力推进、实际上没有任何限制的一条赛道。我想这里不会是那样的情况，但我认为相比蒙扎，在这里你或许确实能带来一些不同的东西。”
detailEn: Why Max Verstappen isn’t buying the hype over a Red Bull surprise in Madrid
Regardless of whether the Madring is a driver’s circuit or not, Verstappen does not think he can single-handedly make the difference for a surprise win

When Max Verstappen was asked during the Dutch media session in Monza whether he now thinks he might not win a single race this Formula 1 season – which would be the first time since his debut year in 2015 – a telling response followed:
"I'm obviously never going to say that out loud!"

Last year, however, Verstappen did say it, and seemingly it worked. After making that statement, the Red Bull driver finished on the podium in every grand prix during the second half of the season and fell just two points short of a fifth consecutive world title.

Verstappen knows better than anyone, however, that the situation is completely different this year and that a turnaround is virtually out of the question. An entire season without a win, for the first time in more than a decade, is therefore a realistic possibility.

"Every time I’m in the car, I always go for the maximum. If the opportunity comes to win a race, then of course I’ll go all out for it. But with how things stand at the moment, that chance isn’t very big."

A new circuit brings additional question marks with it, and attention quickly turns to exceptional drivers such as Verstappen, Fernando Alonso and Lewis Hamilton, who can adapt quickly and gain a competitive advantage.

Verstappen doubts, however, whether he can pull off something special around the IFEMA complex in Madrid, despite the track being described as a circuit where drivers can make more of a difference than at somewhere like Monza.
"I mean, you can make the story as beautiful as you want, right? Driver’s track or not, at the end of the day you still need a fast car in Formula 1."
That applies not only to the Madring, but also to Verstappen’s season in general. The Dutchman believes he is performing at a high level, but that is not reflected in the results.
"As a driver, I feel good this year, but I'm not winning races. Does that mean I'm a bad driver or not quick enough? I don't think so.
"It's not that suddenly because this is more of a driver's track than Monza or whatever, you can do a lot better."
Verstappen is now seriously considering the scenario that he might not win a single race this year

Ahead of the first grand prix at the Madring, much of the discussion has centred on the dangers of the circuit. The F3 test produced no fewer than 19 red flags, while Williams team principal James Vowles described the newest addition to the F1 calendar as ‘a car killer’.
Asked by Motorsport.com whether the Madring is really that dangerous, Verstappen replied:
"Well, it could be. In some places, when you have a tiny moment, it can result in a crash. But I mean, Jeddah is the same and we've spoken about that already before.
"You just have to deal with it and try to figure out the margins, to try and keep it under control. But of course, when you're on the limit, it's easy to make a little mistake."
Verstappen mentions Jeddah for a reason. In his view, that is the closest comparison to the Madring, as another street circuit where every mistake is punished severely.
"In terms of what I feel, yes. Of course, there are quite a lot more lower speed corners here, but the sensation I get is a little bit like that, yeah."
Both Verstappen and Lawson compare the Madring with the street circuit in Jeddah
Red Bull stand-in and temporary team-mate Liam Lawson sees that comparison as well, particularly because of the many blind corners that characterise both tracks.
"The way these street circuits are built, the walls just sort of follow where the track goes and they're just very blind in a lot of places", said the New Zealander on Thursday.

"There are a lot of faster flowing corners where you have something behind it and you can't see it. Jeddah obviously has more of that than this place, but it's sort of similar in that way, I would say."
Many parts of the Madring can catch drivers out, but the chicane formed by Turns 5 and 6 certainly looks like one of the trickiest.

"If you take too much of the first kerb, it'll bounce you across the second kerb, which will then bounce you into the wall. Trying to be accurate through a section like that is quite tough", Lawson admitted.

"I've seen a lot of videos of F3 cars just smashing both the kerbs and getting away with it, or not getting away with it, so it's definitely a tricky part of the track. The braking zone is obviously not straight as well, so trying not to lock and push that braking zone is going to be pretty tough."
Finally, Lawson does not think drivers will be able to push completely to the limit in Madrid without feeling the limitations of the 2026 power units.

"Not like Monaco, no. I think Monaco is one where we can push flat out and actually have no limitations. I would say this is not going to be like that, but I think it definitely is somewhere that, more so than in Monza, you can probably make a bit of a difference."

items.titleZh: F1车手展望首次驶上“疯狂”的马德里赛道赛道
items.summaryZh: F1车手准备周五首次驾驶“吓人”且“疯狂”的马德里赛道赛道，预计它将成为本赛季“最复杂”的赛道。
items.originalTitle: F1车手展望首次驶上“疯狂”的Madring赛道
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 drivers are bracing to drive the "scary" and "crazy" Madring circuit for the first time on Friday, with expectations that it will be the "most complicated" track of the year.
detailZh: F1车手们正准备在周五首次驾驶“吓人”且“疯狂”的马德里赛道赛道，预计它将成为本赛季“最复杂”的赛道。
所有F1车手都已经在虚拟世界中完成了许多圈，为三年来第一条全新赛道做准备，但周四让他们近距离看到了赛道在现实世界中的样子。
以下是车手们的期望，从最艰难的弯道到是否错失了改善超车的机会。
两周前在该赛道进行的为期两天的F3测试产生了19次红旗，提高了人们对疯狂周末的期望，威廉姆斯车队负责人James Vowles称其为“杀死赛车的赛道”。
“当我听说F3中有20[19]次红旗时，我有点惊讶。然后在我驾驶模拟器后，我惊讶于只有20[19]次红旗，”梅赛德斯车手拉塞尔打趣道。
“这是一条疯狂的赛道。我会说，它可以说是整个赛历中最危险的赛道。”
赛道上布满了棘手的弯道、盲区出口和靠近的墙壁，几乎没有犯错的空间。博托莱托将马德里赛道的一圈描述为“精神上令人疲惫”。
刚走完赛道的阿尔本表示，“很多墙壁，很多高速弯道，很多盲弯给我一种澳门的氛围，但更像是为F1赛道准备的”。
“有些弯道的盲区有点令人担忧，比如如果有一辆车停在弯道的另一侧，我希望他们在VSC[虚拟安全车]和红旗方面能迅速行动，”他补充道。
“不可避免的是，这个周末会有一些撞车事故。”
加斯利对此表示赞同，他说：“我肯定会把赌注押在红旗上”，他预计会有相当“混乱的周末”和事故。
Albon表示，他“相当担心”在倾斜的La Monumental弯道排位赛中赛车将如何让路，考虑到你通过那里的线路和盲区出口。
“我认为没有正确的位置可以放置赛车，”Albon在谈到La Monumental时说。“如果你把车放在顶部，实际上我认为线路会漂移到赛道中间，然后你再回来。
“所以，你不在一个完美的地方。这让我有点想起，你还记得Fernando和Esteban在巴西3号弯的那次撞车吗[2023年冲刺排位赛]？
“你会遇到脏空气，脏空气会产生连锁反应。”
在模拟器运行后，凯迪拉克车手Sergio Perez表示，这是“一条真正的赛道。有点吓人。让我有点想起吉达”。队友Valtteri Bottas将其描述为吉达和巴库的混合体，而其他人则将其比作摩纳哥。
哈斯车手奥康称其为“疯狂的赛道”，需要在风险与回报之间做出许多权衡，而冠军领跑者安东内利表示，这对车手和工程师来说都是今年“最复杂”的赛道。
“从驾驶方面来说，你有各种各样的弯道。你有减速弯、快速弯、倾斜弯、中速弯，还有刹车——你有很多直线刹车，但也有[很多]刹车时你实际上仍在转弯，”Antonelli说。
“17号弯是一个当你踩刹车时，你仍在转弯，然后你拉直赛车的弯道。所以这是一条非常棘手的赛道，非常具有挑战性，但同时非常令人兴奋，零犯错空间。
“在工程方面也很复杂，因为找到一个对整个单圈都是良好妥协的调校并不容易。
“你可以找到一个在减速弯中帮助你、当你需要切路肩时的调校，或者一个在快速弯中帮助你的调校，但要找到一个在路肩上好、在改变方向时好、在快速弯中好的调校，将会很困难。”
人们预计周六的排位赛将非常激烈，但车手们对周日的比赛质量表示了新的担忧。
“超车会很困难。在我看来，会更接近新加坡，”Perez的观点。
不过，Gasly将其视为一个机会。他期待探索超车机会，因为车手们将不得不“在比赛日即兴发挥和创造，看看什么是可能的。
“我们将是这些首次动作的创造者。”
曾希望车手们采取不同线路进入La Monumental弯道会创造超车机会，但Albon并不那么确定。
“我担心比赛中的轮胎碎屑。所以除了试图找到干净空气并试图在倾斜弯道上走高线外，你还要在比赛后期应对轮胎碎屑，所以你必须小心，”Albon说。
“我个人认为你不能走那么多线路。赛道相当狭窄，当你拥有干净空气和空间时情况不同，而如果你有一点打滑，你就会立即撞墙。
“车手们不太愿意把车开到倾斜弯道的顶部并承担走高速线的风险。我希望我被证明是错的，但我认为赛道的那个部分不会提供那么多超车机会。”
哈斯车手Ollie Bearman觉得马德里赛道的布局错失了一个机会。
“在某种程度上这是一种遗憾，因为我认为布局还可以，但赛道有一些特性自然阻碍了超车，”Bearman说。
“其中之一是5号弯的刹车，它是弯曲的——而那是真正的超车机会。那种弯曲刹车消除了任何不同线路和从内侧发送的可能性。
“所以这是一种遗憾，也许有点疏忽，但这意味着我们将完全专注于排位赛。”
5/6号减速弯是F3测试中许多事故的发生地，前面有两个全油门弯道，这也是赛道上仅有的两个直线模式区域之一。
所以进入那个减速弯，以及第一个减速弯，是最合乎逻辑的超车机会。
但是，正如Bearman所说，进入减速弯的入口是弯曲且狭窄的，所以超车真的必须在刹车区之前完成。
Albon也有同样的挫败感，他认为周日的任何超车都将由能量管理差异决定，而不是刹车差异。
“我希望他们在刹车区做了一些不同的东西，不要让它们太倾斜，”Albon说。
“你有很多组合弯道，仅仅考虑周日的超车，感觉很容易防守。你只需把车放在赛道中间，就不会有车能超过你。
“这只是意味着这将是更多的部署超车而不是刹车超车。”
detailEn: Formula 1 drivers are bracing to drive the "scary" and "crazy" Madring circuit for the first time on Friday, with expectations that it will be the "most complicated" track of the year.

All F1 drivers have completed many laps in the virtual world to prepare for the first brand-new track in three years, but Thursday gave them their up-close look at how the circuit has come together in the real-world.
Here’s what the drivers are expecting, from the toughest corners to whether there was a missed opportunity to improve overtaking.

A two-day Formula 3 test at the circuit produced 19 red flags two weeks ago, raising expectations of a frenetic weekend, with Williams team principal James Vowles calling it "a track that kills cars".
"When I heard about the 20 [19] red flags in F3, I was a bit surprised. And then after I drove on the sim, I was surprised there was only 20 [19] red flags," quipped Mercedes driver George Russell.
"It's a crazy circuit. I would put it, arguably, as the most risky circuit of the whole calendar."
The circuit is littered with tricky corners, blind exits and close walls that leave very little room for error. "Mentally exhausting" is how Gabriel Bortoleto described a lap of the Madring.
Fresh from walking the track, Alex Albon said there's "a lot of walls, a lot of high-speed corners, a lot of blind corners gives me vibes of Macau, but more for an F1 track".

"A little bit concerning the blind spots in some of the corners, like if there is a car that's stopped on the other side of the corner, I hope they're just quick on the VSCs [virtual safety cars] and the red flags," he added.
"Inevitably, there are going to be a few crashes this weekend."
Pierre Gasly echoed that, saying, "I'll put my money on the red flag, that's for sure", and he expects quite a "disrupted weekend" with accidents.
Albon said he is "quite concerned" about where cars will get out of the way in qualifying at the banked La Monumental corner, given the line you take through there and the blind exit.

"I don't think there's a correct place you can position the car," Albon said of La Monumental. “If you put the car up top, actually I think the line is kind of drift up to the middle of the track and then you come back again.
"So, you're not in a perfect place. It reminds me a little bit of, do you remember Fernando and Esteban in Brazil at Turn 3, where they had that crash [in sprint qualifying in 2023]?
"You can get dirty air and the dirty air can create the knock-on effect."

After his simulator running, Cadillac driver Sergio Perez said it was "a proper track. It's a bit scary. It reminds me a bit of Jeddah". Team-mate Valtteri Bottas described it as a mix between Jeddah and Baku, while others have compared it to Monaco.

Haas driver Esteban Ocon called it a "crazy circuit" with so much risk versus reward trade-offs to make, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli said it's the "most complicated" track of the year for both drivers and engineers.

"Driving-wise, you've got all kinds of corners. You've got chicanes, fast corners, banked, medium-speed, also braking - you've got a lot of straight-line braking, but [also] a lot of braking where you're actually still turning," Antonelli said.

"Turn 17 is a corner where, when you hit the brake, you're still turning, and then you straighten the car. So it's a very tricky track, very challenging, but very exciting at the same time with zero margin of mistake.
"It's also complicated on the engineering side because finding a set-up that is a good compromise for the whole lap is not going to be easy.

"You can find a set-up that helps you in the chicanes, when you need to cut kerbs, or a set-up that helps you in the fast corners, but to find a set-up that is good over kerbs, good on changing direction, good on fast corners, is going to be difficult."
There are expectations for a knife-edge qualifying on Saturday, but drivers have expressed fresh concerns about the quality of racing on Sunday.
"Overtaking will be hard. It's going to be, in my mind, closer to Singapore," was Perez's view.
Gasly saw it as an opportunity, though. He was relishing exploring the overtaking opportunities, as drivers will have to "improvise and be creative on race day and see what's possible.
"We'll be the creators of these first moves."
There had been hopes that drivers taking different lines into the La Monumental corner would create an overtaking opportunity, but Albon isn’t so sure.

"I worry about the marbles in the race. So on top of trying to find clean air and trying to go up high on the banking, you'll have marbles to contend with as well later into the race, so you've got to be careful with that," Albon said.

"I personally don't think you can do that many lines. The track's quite narrow and it's different when you have clean air and there's space, whereas if you have a little snap you're into the wall immediately.

"Drivers aren't as willing to stick it up to the top of the banking and take the risk of running a high line. I hope I'm proved wrong, but I think that part of the track is not going to offer that much overtaking."
Haas driver Ollie Bearman felt like an opportunity was missed with the layout of the Madring.
"It's a shame in a way because I think the layout is OK, but there are some features of the circuit which naturally deter overtaking," Bearman said.

"One of them is the braking for Turn 5, which is curved - and that's the real overtaking opportunity. That kind of curved braking takes away any possibility of different lines and sending one up the inside.
"So that's a shame and maybe a bit of an oversight, but it means that we're going to be fully focused on qualifying."
The Turn 5/6 chicane, the site of many accidents in the F3 test, is preceded by two flat-out kinks, which also feature one of only two straight mode zones on the circuit.
So into that chicane, along with the first chicane, is the most logical overtaking opportunity.
But, as Bearman said, the entry to the chicane is curved and tight, so the overtakes will really have to be completed before the braking zone.
Albon shares his frustration, believing any overtakes on Sunday will be decided by energy management differences rather than braking differences.
"I wish they did something a bit different with the braking zones and not having them too much angled," Albon said.

"You've got a lot of combined corners which, just thinking of overtaking on Sunday, it feels like it's quite easy to defend. You just put the car in the middle of the track and you're not going to get a car that's going to go past you.
"That just means that it will be more of a deployment overtake than a braking overtake."

items.originalTitle: 法拉利车手透露蒙扎赛后会谈内容
items.summaryEn: Ferrari Formula 1 drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc say they have cleared the air after their opening-lap Italian Grand Prix squabble, and they will continue to race without rules of engagement for now.
detailZh: 法拉利F1车手汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔声称，在意大利大奖赛首圈争执后，他们已经澄清了情况——目前他们将继续在没有交战规则的情况下比赛。
Hamilton在蒙扎1号弯从内线猛冲超越Leclerc，但在2号弯两人激烈缠斗时，他发现自己冲入了砂石地。
Leclerc赛后说“我们做得太过分了”，Hamilton对此言论不太高兴，他说：“2号弯时我在前面。到弯心时，我在前面。所以这里面没有‘我们’。”
但Hamilton表示，他们事后互相交谈以澄清情况。
“很棒的是，我们没有回避讨论。我们面对面坐着，只有他和我在那里，谈了这件事，”Hamilton周四在马德里解释道。
“我们都很开放和诚实，我们解决了问题，可以继续前进。我认为这显示了他的成熟，我认为这是健康的。这是我们随着时间建立起来的关系。
“当然，会有沮丧的时候，我相信还会有更多我们接近的时候，因为我们的速度非常接近。我们都想赢，也都想为车队做好。但是的，我认为这是非常积极的。”
Leclerc则表示，“很明显，我们永远不想看到同一车队的赛车在草地上。”
“所以，是的，我的意思是，回顾之后，我们和Lewis谈了。我当然知道我在2号弯做得太过分了，我对Lewis说了，我认为我们未来应该做什么或避免什么非常清楚。
“但我不会比我们已经说的透露更多细节。我唯一能说的是，这绝对没有影响我们之间的良好关系，也不会影响未来的任何事情。这对我来说才是最重要的，真的。
“当这些事情发生在我们的主场比赛中时，确实会在外面引起巨大的混乱。然而，我的意思是，从外面看比赛，其他队友之间也有一些摩擦。
“人们最终只谈论Lewis和我，我认为这不太对。但这并不意味着我们做的一切都很完美。我在2号弯就没有。
“为此，在回顾图像后，我立即对Lewis非常明确地说了。”
Leclerc再次强调，法拉利车手受到了不成比例的关注，而其他队友也在激烈争斗。
“再说一次，我需要小心，因为这不是要淡化事情的发展方式，看到Lewis冲入砂石地等是不可接受的，”Leclerc说。
“但可以肯定的是，事实上，我们这边的比例比其他两支车队要大得多……我没有看完整场比赛……但我看到其他两支在顶部争斗的车队，周围的噪音没有那么多。
“所以，当你为法拉利开车时，事情的比例肯定要大得多，尤其是在蒙扎。但这并不是要淡化发生的事情。这不是应该再次发生的事情。”
蒙扎之后，有消息透露法拉利车手之间“没有规则”，这让人非常惊讶。
Hamilton在蒙扎后的周一与车队老板Fred Vasseur进行了交谈，此前他在赛后媒体采访中大部分时间都在呼吁法拉利对其运营和执行周末的方式做出重大改变。
“这真的很积极，”Hamilton谈到蒙扎之后的日子时说。
“我周一和Fred谈了，我们只是在澄清……讨论……自然，我们总是会有不同的意见，但最终，我们走到一起，找到前进的道路。
“这就是过去15个月左右我们取得的积极进展。我们已经达到了内部沟通非常好的地步，我和Charles之间也是如此。”
当被问及引入交战规则——类似于Hamilton在梅赛德斯期间一直有的——是否是那些与Vasseur对话的一部分时，Hamilton说“不是”。
当被问及为什么不是时，Hamilton回答说：“现在我只是试图专注于这个周末有一个更好的周末。
“我相信在某个阶段我们会讨论如何做得更好，但我们没有太多时间扭转局面。你不可能在两天内改变事情。”
当The 比赛问及法拉利是否能迅速实施Hamilton在蒙扎后呼吁的那种沟通和程序变革时，他回答说：“我认为这是一个长期的过程。这不是我们这个周末就能改变的。
“有大量的变动部分。有很多人。有一种存在了很长时间的文化。移动大块的东西并不容易。
“我们只是一步一步来。它从讨论开始。它从承认开始，我们在内部已经承认了。
“然后就是一起找出解决方案。这不会一夜之间发生。我们可能会尝试一些事情，仍然不会好，但我们最终会达到我们需要的地步。”
Hamilton继续公开坚称，他在法拉利呼吁的任何改变都不包括要求车队优先考虑他而不是Leclerc。相反，这一切都是为了确保车队团结一致，以便利用梅赛德斯的任何失误。
“我的意思是，这实际上并不是我一直在要求的，”他说。
“这真的只是确保我们执行，以确保我们为车队取得最好的结果，而不是我们互相争斗，最终获得第四和第五。
“也许你们可以合作，获得一个领奖台，拿到更多积分。我认为在这一点上，
“梅赛德斯，如果你看上一场比赛，在直道上每圈快了十分之六。几乎在大多数其他赛道上，我们在直道上就损失了十分之三或十分之四。
“所以我认为，考虑到我们有那样的劣势，我们做得非常出色，我们继续改进赛车。我们对引擎进行了改进。我们知道最后一次升级不会是银弹，完全弥补那个差距。但对我来说，看到我们不断前进是非常积极的，他们只是非常非常快，这并不容易。
“所以正如我所说，与其关注他们，他们目前不是我的焦点。我认为我们的焦点应该只是我们如何在自己的周末做到最好、执行得最好，因为会有他们表现出色的周末，也会有他们可能失误的周末。
“只要我们专注于我们的稳定性，努力优化我们的周末，也许会有某个时刻我们能够利用他们的缺点。”
detailEn: Ferrari Formula 1 drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc claim they've cleared the air after their opening lap Italian Grand Prix squabble - and they'll continue to race without rules of engagement for now.
Hamilton dived down the inside of Leclerc at Turn 1 at Monza but found himself in the gravel at Turn 2 as they battled each other hard.
Leclerc said "we went too far" after the race, a remark Hamilton wasn't too pleased about saying "I was ahead in Turn 2. By the apex, I was ahead. So there was no 'we' in it."
But Hamilton said they spoke to each other afterwards to clear the air.
"What's great is that there was no shying away from having a discussion. We sat face-to-face, just him and I and talked about it," Hamilton explained on Thursday in Madrid.
"We were just both open and honest and we squashed it and we can move on. I think that shows the maturity from him and I think it's healthy. It's a relationship we have built over time.

"Of course, there's going to be frustrations and I'm sure there'll be more times where we're close because we're very close in pace. We both want to win just as much as each other and we both want to do well for the team as well. But yeah, I think it's a real positive."
For his part, Leclerc said it's "clear that we never want to see a car of the same team in the grass.
"So yeah, I mean, after reviewing, we spoke with Lewis. I obviously know I went too far in Turn 2 and I said it to Lewis and I think it's very clear what we should do or should avoid going forward.

"But I won't go into much more detail than what we've said. The only thing I can say is that it definitely did not affect the good relationship that we have and it will not affect anything going forward. And that is the most important for me, really.
"When these things happen at our home race, then it does [make] a huge mess outside. However, I mean, looking at the race from outside, there's also been some friction between other team-mates.
"The only thing [people] end up speaking of is Lewis and I, which I don't think is quite right. But that doesn't mean we did everything perfectly. I didn't in Turn 2.
"And for that, I've been straight away very clear with Lewis after reviewing the images."
Leclerc doubled down on this assertion that a disproportionate focus had been placed on the Ferrari drivers, when other team-mates had been fighting each other hard too.
"Again, I need to be careful with that because it's not to minimise the way that this unfolded, it's not acceptable to see Lewis going in the gravel, etc." Leclerc said.

"But for sure, the proportions, as a matter of fact, are much bigger on our side compared to the two other teams that have had some…I didn't follow the whole race…but the two other teams I saw that were fighting at the top, there wasn't as much noise around it.

"So surely the proportions that it takes when you are driving for Ferrari is much bigger and particularly if we're in Monza. But that's not to minimise what happened. It's not something that should happen again."
There was much surprise after Monza when it was revealed the Ferrari drivers have "no rules" for racing each other.

Hamilton spoke to team boss Fred Vasseur on the Monday after Monza, having spent much of his post-race media sessions calling for Ferrari to make big changes to the way it operates and executes its weekends.
It's been really positive," Hamilton said of the days after Monza.
"I spoke to Fred on Monday, and we're just clearing up…discussion of…naturally, we're going to always have different opinions, but at the end of the day, we come together and we find a way forward.
"That's the positives of where we've got to over the past 15 months or whatever it is. We've got to a place where we have really great communication internally, and the same with me and Charles."
Asked if the introduction of rules of engagement - similar to what Hamilton had throughout his time at Mercedes - was part of those conversations with Vasseur, Hamilton said "It was not".
Asked why they weren't, Hamilton replied: "Right now I'm just trying to focus on having a better weekend, this weekend.
"I'm sure at some stage we'll discuss how we can be better, but we've not had a lot of time to turn around. You can't change things in two days."

Asked by The Race if Ferrari could quickly implement the kind of communication and procedural changes Hamilton was calling for after Monza, he replied: "I think it's a longer-term process. It's not something we can just change into this weekend.
"There's a huge amount of moving parts. There's a lot of people. There's a culture that's been there for a long, long time. Moving big pieces is not so easy.
"We just take it one step at a time. It starts with discussing it. It starts with the acknowledgement, which internally we have.
"Then it just comes to working out solutions together. It just doesn't happen overnight. We'll probably try things and it still won't be good, but we'll eventually get to the point we need."

Hamilton continues to insist publicly that any change he's calling for at Ferrari doesn't include asking the team to prioritise him over Leclerc. Instead it's all about ensuring the team all pulls together so it can make the most of any slip-ups from Mercedes.
"I mean, that's not actually really what I've been asking for," he said.
"It's really just making sure we're executing to make sure we get the best result for the team instead of us working against each other and finishing fourth and fifth.
"Maybe you can work together and get a podium and pull off more points. I think at this point,
"Mercedes, if you look at the last race, there was six tenths of a lap quicker on the straights. Pretty much most of the other tracks, there's three or four tenths we're losing just on the straights.

"So I think we've done a really great job given that we've had that deficit and we continue to make improvements to the car. We've made improvements to the engine. We knew that the last upgrade wasn't going to be a silver bullet and close that gap completely. But for me, it's really positive to see us continuously stepping forward and they are just very, very quick and it's not easy.

"So as I said, rather than focus on them, they're not a focus for me at the moment. I think our focus should just be how we can do the best and execute the best on our weekends because there'll be weekends where they're exceptional and there'll be weekends where they maybe drop the ball.
"As long as we just focus on our consistency and trying to optimise our weekends, maybe there's going to be a moment where we are able to capitalise on perhaps their shortcomings."

"最重要的是先进行沟通。我在法拉利已经待了这么多年，我知道当法拉利的一切仿佛都着火时是什么感觉，如果我和刘易斯之间不沟通，你就可能被围绕车队的这种喧嚣所困扰，"勒克莱尔说。

"我和刘易斯谈过了。我们一直有着很好的关系。我非常尊重刘易斯。我告诉他，在2号弯，我的行为不像我应有的样子，也不像一个队友应有的样子。

这场蒙扎的碰撞是汉密尔顿与勒克莱尔自去年年初成为队友以来最高调的一次事故。
汉密尔顿经历过多次与队友在赛道上的交锋，包括与简森·巴顿、尼科·罗斯伯格和乔治·拉塞尔，他表示他已经与勒克莱尔“化解”了这次事件，“所以不会留下任何芥蒂”。
“我认为很棒的一点是，我们没有回避讨论。我们面对面坐着，只有他和我，就此进行了交谈，我们都坦诚开放，把这件事化解了，我们可以继续前行，”他说。
"我认为这体现了他成熟的一面，我觉得这是健康的。这是我们长期以来建立起来的一种关系。当然，难免会有沮丧的时候，而且我相信以后还会有更多我们近距离交锋的时刻，因为我们的速度非常接近。我们俩都想赢得比赛，也同样都想为车队取得好成绩。"
卡伦·钱多克就刘易斯·汉密尔顿的说法发表了自己的看法。汉密尔顿称，队友夏尔·勒克莱尔跑偏出弯，迫使他驶出赛道，把他留在了砂石地和路肩上，并让他损失了好几个位置。
汉密尔顿曾要求在与勒克莱尔比赛时制定交战规则，就像他在梅赛德斯时那样，但他透露这并不是蒙扎赛后讨论的一部分。
"现在，我只是想专注于让这个周末过得更好，"他说。
"我相信在某个阶段我们会讨论如何做得更好，但我们没有太多时间来扭转局面。你不可能在两天内改变一切。"

detailZh: 本周末举办西班牙大奖赛的新马德里赛道赛道是F1自2023年拉斯维加斯以来首条全新赛道。
虽然它官方上也是街道赛道，因为它围绕马德里主要机场附近的IFEMA展览中心区域运行，但其中一半更像是永久性场地，因为它蜿蜒通向标志性的La Monumental倾斜弯。
海拔变化也令人印象深刻——仅从7号弯到8号弯就有8%的上坡坡度——在现实中看起来比照片中可能更加壮观。
虽然车手们还有24小时才能正式上赛道，但一些清晰的初步印象已经浮现，显示出为什么F1正在为可能充满挑战的周末做准备。
马德里赛道最受关注的弯角当然是La Monumental的倾斜弯。
自从赛道最初设计公布以来，它就吸引了人们的注意，车手、车队和轮胎供应商倍耐力都公开表示这是本赛季技术难度最高的弯角。
在施工期间它看起来就很壮观，但随着这个约550米长的弯角的赛道工程完工，它现在看起来更加惊艳。
看台高耸其上，内侧还建造了巨大的招待区域，给人一种类似圆形剧场的感觉，让人想起英特拉格斯起终点直道的紧张感。
现在关键是要了解那里是否有多种赛车线路可供选择，从而让它变得更好。
马德里赛道周围有很多地方有可能让车手犯错。
有La Monumental，还有17号右弯，车手在之前快速左弯后必须大力刹车，这将相当棘手。
但根据F3测试的证据，并由赛道上仍然留下的轮胎痕迹所证明，5/6号弯的减速弯可能是主要麻烦点。
它位于赛道最快点的末端——从3号弯开始的长弯道段——车手必须应对一个相当棘手的减速弯。
路肩需要谨慎对待，但出口处护栏的角度——形成了一个收窄点——很可能让很多人吃亏。
虽然街道赛道过去常有颠簸路面问题，但马德里赛道非常平滑。
绕赛道走一圈可以看出，铺设的沥青应该不会给赛车带来什么问题，不需要为了提高离地间隙而调整以应对意外的起伏。
在赛道限制方面，很多地方的墙壁形成了赛道的自然边缘，但有些地方设置了涂漆路肩以让车手远离混凝土。
为了帮助车手保持在白线内，FIA使用了在吉达、迈阿密和奥斯汀等地使用的小型涂漆肋线来辅助。
每个到达马德里赛道的人都面临的一个冒险是试图在F1围场中辨认方向——因为它大得离谱。
车库必须被安置进IFEMA展览中心建筑群，这意味着独特的布局。
不是一排长长的车库彼此相邻，而是在威廉姆斯和小红牛之间有一个150米的空隙——媒体和电视区被安排在那里。
车库后面也有相当独特的情况，卡车和工程办公室设在那里。（招待单元有自己独立的区域）。
由于IFEMA建筑群的布局，一些车队被安排进有空调的建筑，而其他车队——如迈凯伦和梅赛德斯——则在户外的炎热中。
车队之间也有一些不寻常的间隔。在威廉姆斯和小红牛之间行走，这两支车队在围场中通常紧挨着，却需要超过两分钟。
维修区很长，出口很棘手
由于扩展的维修车库建筑群布局，维修区很长——非常非常长。
两个限速线之间维修区的官方距离是562米。
出去的路上也有相当多的额外距离——这将相当棘手，因为赛车将加速冲向右侧的混凝土护栏，然后在3号弯出口汇入。
F1轮胎供应商倍耐力估计时间损失约为25秒——部分原因是维修区不是在第一个弯角重新汇入，而是在3号弯出口。
detailEn: The new Madring circuit that hosts this weekend’s Spanish Grand Prix is Formula 1’s first new circuit since Las Vegas in 2023.

While officially also a street circuit, as it runs around the IFEMA Exhibition Centre space near Madrid's main airport, half of it is more like a permanent venue as it winds its way towards the iconic La Monumental banked turn.
The elevation change is impressive too - with an 8% gradient uphill from Turn 7 to Turn 8 alone - looking even more spectacular in real life than it probably does in photos.

While drivers still have another 24 hours to go before they take to the track proper, some clear first impressions have emerged that show why F1 is bracing itself for what could be a challenging weekend.
The most talked about corner at the Madring is of course the banked corner at La Monumental.

It has grabbed attention ever since the first designs of the track were revealed, and drivers, teams and tyre supplier Pirelli have talked openly about it being the most technically demanding of the season.
It looked impressive when under construction but, with track work now complete around the 550-metre-long turn, it looks even more stunning now.

With grandstands towering high above it, and a huge hospitality area having been constructed on the inside, there is something akin to an amphitheatre feel to it that is reminiscent of the intensity of the start-finish straight at Interlagos.
Now the key thing to understand is whether there are multiple racing lines on offer through there that could make it even better.
There are plenty of places around Madring that have potential to catch drivers out.
There is La Monumental, plus the Turn 17 right-hander, where drivers have to brake heavily while navigating a quick left sweep beforehand, is going to be quite a handful.
But based on evidence from F3 testing, and proven by the tyre marks still left on the track, it is the Turn 5/6 chicane that could be the main trouble point.
Coming at the end of the quickest point of the track – the long sweeping section from Turn 3 – drivers have to negotiate a quite tricky chicane.
The kerbs will require treating with caution, but it is the angle of the barrier on the exit – which offers a pinch point – that could well be what catches a lot of people out.
While street circuits have had a habit in the past of throwing up problems with bumpy surfaces, Madring is super smooth.
A walk around the track has shown that the asphalt put down should pose few problems for cars in needing to raise ride heights to adjust from some unexpected undulations.
In terms of track limits, the walls form a natural edge to the circuit in a lot of places, but there are some spots where painted kerbs have been put in to keep drivers away from the concrete.
To help give drivers some guidance to stay within the white lines, the FIA has used little painted rib lines that are utilised at places like Jeddah, Miami and Austin to help assist.
One of the adventures everyone arriving at Madring has faced is trying to get their bearings around the F1 paddock – because it is bonkers big.
The garages have had to be fitted into the IFEMA exhibition centre complex and that has meant a unique layout.
Rather than being one long line of garages next to each other, there is a 150-metre gap in the middle between Williams and Racing Bulls – where the media and TV pen has been slotted in.
There is also quite a unique situation behind the garages too, where the trucks and engineering offices are based. (The hospitality units have their own separate area).
Because of the layout of the IFEMA complex, some teams have been slotted into air-conditioned buildings, while others – like McLaren and Mercedes – are outside in the heat.
There are also some unusual gaps between teams. Walking between Williams and Racing Bulls, who are normally right next to each in the paddock, takes more than two minutes.
The pitlane is long and the exit is tricky
Thanks to the extended pit garage complex layout, the pitlane is long – very, very long.
The official distance of the pitlane between the two speed limiter lines is 562 metres.

There is quite a bit of extra distance on the way out too – which is going to be quite tricky to negotiate as cars are going to accelerate towards a right-hand concrete barrier before they blend in at the exit of Turn 3.
F1 tyre supplier Pirelli estimates that the time loss will be around 25 seconds – helped in part by the pitlane not rejoining at the first turn but instead coming out at Turn 3.

items.titleZh: 法拉利可借鉴迈凯伦与梅赛德斯车手管理经验
items.summaryZh: 法拉利正面临勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿之间的车手关系问题，Jon Noble撰文指出，法拉利可以从迈凯伦和梅赛德斯处理车手关系的政策中汲取经验。

media.altZh: 法拉利可借鉴迈凯伦与梅赛德斯车手管理经验

items.originalTitle: 法拉利可从两大对手借鉴的车手管理经验
items.summaryEn: Ferrari is facing a driver relationship issue between Leclerc and Hamilton, and Jon Noble argues that Ferrari can learn from how McLaren and Mercedes have handled their driver relationships.
detailZh: 毫无疑问，法拉利现在需要就如何最好地处理其F1车手关系做出决定。
蒙扎第一个减速弯发生的事件所错失的机会，加上刘易斯·汉密尔顿对缺乏比赛规则和团队配合的沮丧，意味着领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔并非看不到采取行动的必要性。
正如瓦塞尔在意大利大奖赛周日晚间所确认的，回应即将到来。
“按理说，你必须在某个阶段做出决定，”他说。“每支车队都不同。但你必须做出决定，我们[将]决定。”
瓦塞尔选择走哪条路尚不清楚——因为摆在桌面上的选项很多。
一个极端是把一切资源都押在汉密尔顿身上，让他作为积分榜上的领头车手，以尽量最大化法拉利正在消退的争冠机会。
这是最不可能的选择，因为这不是汉密尔顿明确要求的事情。
在勒克莱尔从数学上尚未退出争冠的时候，强行这样做对他也是一颗难以下咽的苦药。
其他选择包括商定明确的交战规则，甚至干脆选择让事情照旧进行，信任车手们自己处理好。
但如果从法拉利的对手如何处理类似情况中可以明确一件事，那就是这里没有能让所有人都满意的简单解决方案。
正如迈凯伦领队安德烈亚·斯特拉多次提到处理车手关系时所说的，不可能制定出一个既符合车手个人利益又符合车队利益的框架。
“我总是和车手们讨论，这是我们职业生涯中将要面对的最困难的事情，”他几年前告诉我。
“这是唯一一件我们无法通过让利益完全一致来面对的事情。”
近年来，迈凯伦在管理兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里方面遇到了不少头疼问题，著名的“木瓜规则”多次被推到极限。
允许两位车手竞争但严格禁止接触的简单立场看似足够直接，但仍不足以避免所有争议。
2024年匈牙利和蒙扎的糟糕下午，以及去年的意大利大奖赛，暴露了当维修墙对车手的期望与车手个人意愿从未完美契合时所面临的挑战规模。
此外，协议会被推到极限，车队随后有义务对违规行为施加回应——正如去年新加坡大奖赛轮对轮碰撞后诺里斯短暂面临后果那样。
虽然迈凯伦有时受到批评——尤其是在2024年蒙扎之后——因为在本可以更好地全力支持一位车手的时候仍坚持“木瓜规则”，但瓦塞尔在蒙扎之后指出，平等对待对他的对手的争冠目标比早早选择一号车手更有利。
“去年，皮亚斯特里在这个阶段领先迈凯伦，”瓦塞尔在蒙扎之后谈到走支持其中一位车手的路线时说。
“如果迈凯伦把一切押在皮亚斯特里身上，马克斯·维斯塔潘就会成为冠军。”
不过，瓦塞尔关于不支持皮亚斯特里是迈凯伦（与诺里斯）夺冠关键的观点值得商榷，因为如果那样做，后续事件会以不同方式展开。
全力支持皮亚斯特里很可能会改变其他比赛的结果，尤其是避免导致皮亚斯特里巴库困境的意外，以及新加坡和奥斯汀冲刺赛中影响最终积分的碰撞。
不过，“木瓜规则”做了一件事，就是作为一个锚点，保持了一定的团结。
即使在去年那样激烈的冠军争夺之后，两位车手都没有因为处理方式而留下挥之不去的紧张情绪——这让迈凯伦得以在没有任何恶化问题的情况下进入2026年。
但这并不意味着，即使像这样稳固的框架也是避免赛道上紧张的梦想门票。
上周末在意大利，比赛的自由为诺里斯晚些时候在无线电中的一些抱怨打开了大门，他觉得自己在与皮亚斯特里争夺时被挤上了草地。
斯特拉表示，即使在达成一致框架多年之后，情况也会不断产生审查的需要。
“即使我们在2025年以基于平等、让他们比赛、公平等重要原则的竞赛方式赢得了两个冠军，但在现实中，将这些原则转化为真正的比赛总是很困难，”他说。
“就像你[在意大利]看到的，我们再次采取了一种偏冒险的方式。我们让他们比赛，结果一辆车的轮子上了草地。这是我们必须审查的事情。
“如果你让他们不要互相竞争，那么兰多会获得第五名，他可能会说，‘但为了公平，我本希望有机会。’所以，这是一个棘手的问题。”
在最好地管理车队利益与每位车手想要的东西之间的冲突方面，似乎核心在于至少每个人都认同所商定的内容。
“我们与车手团结一致很重要，”斯特拉补充道。“我认为一支车队很难说‘这是我们强加的，现在你们适应’。
“你总是希望确保从各方获得贡献。
“但一旦你看到车队利益受到攻击或处于危险之中，那么你可能必须提升博弈水平，从车队角度开始严格起来。这些就是我们处理方式的基础。”
汉密尔顿在意大利大奖赛后最引人注目的言论之一，是关于他和勒克莱尔在比赛时根本“没有规则”。
“我认为这归结为交战规则，”当被问及他希望看到什么时，他说。
“我在梅赛德斯时，我们有书面的交战规则……这里没有规则。我认为这是需要解决的问题，以尝试修复它。”
梅赛德斯的框架是对汉密尔顿和前队友尼科·罗斯伯格之间激烈竞争的回应，他们的竞争有时在赛道上碰撞时爆发。
车队领队托托·沃尔夫此后将框架改进为更关于“比赛意图”，其愿望与迈凯伦的规则类似，即只要不接触，两位车手都可以激烈竞争。
还有一个元素是，如果维修墙觉得车队利益受到损害，他们不怕介入。
detailEn: There is little doubt that Ferrari needs to make a call now about how best to handle its Formula 1 drivers going forward.

The lost opportunity of what happened at the first chicane at Monza, plus Lewis Hamilton's frustrations at a lack of racing rules and team work, means boss Fred Vasseur is not blind to the need for action.
As Vasseur confirmed on Sunday night at the Italian Grand Prix, a response is coming.
"By reason, you have to take a decision at one stage," he said. "Each team is different. But you have to make a decision, and we [will] decide."
What path Vasseur chooses to go down is unclear – because the options on the table are plenty.
At one extreme is throwing everything behind Hamilton as the lead driver in the standings to try to maximise Ferrari's fading title chances.
This is the most unlikely option because it's not something Hamilton has explicitly called for.
Imposing it would also be a bitter pill for Charles Leclerc to swallow at a time when he is not mathematically out of title contention.
Other choices include agreeing clear rules of engagement, or even electing simply to let things carry on as they are and trusting the drivers to get on with it themselves.
But if there is one thing that is crystal clear from how Ferrari's rivals have dealt with similar situations themselves, there is no easy solution here that will keep everyone happy.

As McLaren chief Andrea Stella has referenced many, many times about the handling of drivers, it is impossible to come up with a framework that fits both their own personal interests and that of the team.
"I always discuss with the drivers that this is the most difficult thing we are going to face in our career," he told me several years ago.
"This is the only thing that we cannot face by having our interests exactly matching."
McLaren has faced plenty of headaches in the management of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri over recent years, with the famed 'Papaya Rules' being tested to the limit on many occasions.
The simple stance of allowing both drivers to race but with a strict no contact mandate seemed straightforward enough but still was not enough to avoid all controversy.

Troubled afternoons like Hungary and Monza in 2024, and last year's Italian Grand Prix, exposed the scale of challenges that come when what the pitwall wants and expects from the drivers never lines up perfectly with their own individual desires.

Plus, agreements get tested to the max and the team then has a duty to impose responses to breaches – as happened after the Singapore GP wheel banging last year when Norris briefly faced repercussions.

While McLaren faced criticisms at times – especially after Monza 2024 – for keeping 'Papaya Rules' in place on occasions when it could have been better to throw everything behind one driver, Vasseur noted after Monza that equality proved better for his rival's title aspirations than having swooped early to choose a number one.
"Last year, Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season," said Vasseur after Monza about going down a route that would back one of his drivers.
"If McLaren put everything on Piastri, Max Verstappen would have been champion."
Vasseur's point about not backing Piastri being key to McLaren winning the title (with Norris) is debatable though, as subsequent events would have played out differently had it done so.

Throwing its weight behind Piastri would likely have changed results at other races, and in particular avoided the upset that caused Piastri's Baku troubles, and collisions in Singapore and the Austin sprint that impacted the final points tally.
'Papaya Rules' has done one thing though in acting as an anchor point in keeping some unity in play.

Even after an intense title fight like last year, there have been no lingering tensions from either driver over how things were handled – which has allowed McLaren to roll into 2026 without any festering troubles.
But this does not mean that even a solid framework like that is a dream ticket to avoid tension on track.
In Italy last weekend, the freedom to race opened the door for some Norris radio complaints late on after he felt he had been pushed onto the grass as he battled with Piastri.
Stella said even after many years of an agreed framework, circumstances throw up the need for constant review.

"Even if in 2025 we achieved both championships with an approach to racing which was based on some important principles of equality, let them race, fairness, in reality, it's always difficult to translate these principles into real racing," he said.

"Like if you see [in Italy], we took again an approach which is on the risky side. We let them race, and we ended up with one car having the wheels on the grass. Something that we will have to review.
"If you ask them not to race each other, then Lando finishes fifth, and he may say, 'But for fairness, I would have liked to have my opportunities.' So, it's a tricky matter."
What seems central to best managing the conflict between team interest and what each driver wants is at least everyone buying into what is agreed.
"It's important that we go united with the drivers," added Stella. "I think it's difficult for a team to say 'this is what we impose, now you guys adapt'.
"You always want to make sure that you get a contribution from all the parties.

"But as soon as you see that the team interest is under attack or is in danger, then you might have to elevate the game and start to be strict from a team point of view. These are the foundation of how we approach it."
One of Hamilton's most striking remarks after the Italian GP was about there being 'no rules' in play at all between himself and Leclerc when it came to racing.
"I think it comes down to rules of engagement," he said when asked about what he wanted to see.
"When I was at Mercedes, we had a written rule of engagement… here there are no rules. I think that's something that needs to be addressed to try and fix that."
The Mercedes framework was a response to the intense rivalry between Hamilton and former team-mate Nico Rosberg that boiled over at times when they collided on track.

Team boss Toto Wolff has since refined the framework to be more about 'racing intent', where the desire is like McLaren's rules in that both drivers can battle hard as long as they don't make contact.
There is also an element of the pitwall not being afraid to intervene if it feels that the team interests are being hurt.
keyPointsZh: 瓦塞尔确认将在某个阶段做出决定，但具体路径尚不明确。
迈凯伦的“木瓜规则”允许车手竞争但禁止接触，仍多次引发争议。
汉密尔顿表示在梅赛德斯时有书面交战规则，而在法拉利没有规则。
keyPointsEn: Vasseur confirmed a decision will be made at some stage, but the specific path remains unclear.
McLaren's 'Papaya Rules' allow drivers to race but forbid contact, yet still sparked controversy multiple times.
Hamilton said there was a written rule of engagement at Mercedes, but there are no rules at Ferrari.

items.titleZh: 奥迪首位F1青训车手有望延续夺冠纪录
items.summaryZh: 随着F1首次亮相马德里，奥迪首位F1青训车手、F3年度冠军领跑者Freddie Slater将在F3冠军争夺战中力争保持其100%的夺冠纪录。
items.originalTitle: 奥迪首位F1青训车手有望延续夺冠纪录
items.summaryEn: As F1 debuts in Madrid, Audi's first F1 protege, Formula 3 championship leader Freddie Slater, will aim to maintain his 100% title-winning streak in the F3 title decider.
detailZh: 随着F1在马德里首秀，奥迪的首位F1新星将在垫场赛——F3冠军决胜战中力争保持自己百分之百的夺冠纪录。
F3领跑者弗雷迪·斯莱特（Freddie Slater）于2026年初成为奥迪F1车手培养计划的首位签约者，这对这家德国制造商来说是一笔重大收获，因为自他在卡丁车生涯中斩获无数奖杯以来，F1车队就一直对他展开争夺。
尽管收到了大量邀请，斯莱特和他的管理团队有意在其职业生涯早期拒绝与F1车队结对——这与马克斯·维斯塔潘和兰多·诺里斯类似，他们都是等到进入F3后才分别接受了红牛和迈凯伦的支持。
"在卡丁车时期可能确实有些吸引力，但在那个时候加入F1车队的计划并不合适，"斯莱特告诉The 比赛。
“我和我的管理团队、我的家人以及我身边的人，我们都知道那不是我职业生涯中合适的时点，因为当时我不需要它。那时候要做的只是在各级赛事中逐步成长。
“但现在，进入F3（三级方程式），这是一个绝佳的机会，让我成长为一名更有经验的车手，并且希望将来能成为F1车手。现在的时机刚刚好。
“对我来说，这里更像一个家，这正是真正吸引我的地方。感觉不像是进入一家公司做生意。
“感觉我真的是加入了一个非常信任我的大家庭，这就是为什么我不会选择其他任何人的原因。”
这位18岁车手自告别卡丁车赛以来的战绩，在目前F1车坛中最令人印象深刻的新秀履历中名列前茅。
他在2023年夺得Ginetta 青训锦标赛冠军，途经20场比赛赢下16场；随后在2024年的意大利F4赛季中又赢下20场比赛中的15场，并夺得总冠军。
此后Slater转战欧洲区域方程式锦标赛（介于F3与F4之间的过渡级别），在20场比赛中赢下8场，进一步印证了他在卡丁车赛时期展现出的所有明星潜质。
这意味着他自告别卡丁车赛以来，在所有全职参赛计划中都保持100%的夺冠纪录；他只曾在短期冬季系列赛或仅以兼职身份参赛的锦标赛中输过。
Slater以积分榜领跑者的身份进入F3马德里站收官战，尽管他是新秀，但他是今年表现最突出的车手。在平均排位赛名次方面，他一直遥遥领先于其他人。
在今年的八场主赛中，他还六次登上领奖台，在蒙扎未能登上领奖台仅仅是因为机械故障。
如果没有那次故障，Trident车手Slater本可以带着巨大的领先优势进入马德里站。相反，他对他唯一的现实争冠对手、前迈凯伦青训车手Ugo Ugochukwu只有微弱的15分优势，而马德里站还有67分可以争夺。
"之前的成功当然会给你信心，人们也会期待很多，但我认为F3是一个非常有趣的赛季，"Slater说。
"很多事情都在发生，而且我还在和很多二年级车手较量[比如Ugochukwu]，他们也都非常出色。
"所以这从来都不可能是一件轻而易举的事。我不得不努力补上大量经验，并非常快地跟上节奏。
"正如你在赛季下半段所看到的，我已经逐渐进入了不错的节奏，显然对赛车的了解也越来越深。
"现在我们正在为总冠军而战，上周日在蒙扎差点就大功告成了，这有点遗憾，但现在我们全力专注于马德里。
Slater说，他学到了"不要试图贪求太多"，因为"在总冠军争夺中，很多时候有些事情并不在你掌控之中"。
他学到了明智的做法是"在必要的时候从第五名拿下一个第四名，而不是试图在比赛中强求太多、想当英雄"。
"作为一名车手，我已经成熟了很多，更多地让比赛向我走来，而不是试图强行制造局面。"
"这绝对是让你有机会赢得总冠军的关键因素之一。"
Slater这个赛季其实还没有经历过一个糟糕的周末，整个赛季他的排位成绩从未跌出前10。最接近的一次是在巴塞罗那，他在那里排位第10，并且最终在主赛中名列第八——但他在那里的冲刺赛中仍然拿到了第二名。
但在那个周末之后，Slater进行了一次重要的调整，这让他得以继续前进并建立起积分榜上的领先优势。
“在摩纳哥和巴塞罗那之后，我和车队一起进行了一次很大程度的重整，”Slater说道。
“车队给了我一辆更适合自己的赛车。随着经验的积累，我也让自己的驾驶风格更加适应F3赛车。我认为这是整个赛季中多种因素结合在一起，让势头逐渐提升了起来。”
这对Slater来说确实奏效了，他在最近四轮比赛中拿到了55分（尽管在蒙扎退赛，并在斯帕与Ugochukwu发生碰撞），而最接近的竞争对手Ugochukwu只拿到了22分。
考虑到F3在那里进行的两天测试中出现了19次红旗，马德里的收官战可能会非常混乱。
Slater谈到马德里时说：“我很喜欢那里。我觉得这条赛道太棒了。我认为它很有个性。它更偏向老派风格。
“所有这些新出现的赛道都很平整、很平坦，开起来感觉没那么刺激。马德里让我想起了澳门和摩纳哥那类赛道，还有英国的Oulton Park，在那里你能真正感受到一些刺激，有颠簸，有真正向你逼近的护墙。”
"这辆车开起来有趣多了。我已经迫不及待想参加周五的排位赛了，那很可能是整个周末最令人兴奋的环节之一。"
但斯莱特（Slater）在驾驶时会不会把积分形势放在心上呢？
"不，不会，这一整年我都是同一个想法。关键在于执行——把成绩最大化,"斯莱特说。
"【在蒙扎】,我们把每一分可能拿到的成绩都做到了极致。有些事情超出我们的控制出了问题，归根结底这就是赛车运动。
"希望我们能有更好的运气，因为今年发生了相当多的事情出了问题，其中很多其实并不在我的掌控之内，把我们置于了不利的局面。
"但就我自己和我目前驾驶的方式而言，我已经处于最高水平的驾驶状态，而且我肯定在证明这一点。
"所以我等不及马德里站了，现在要做的就是最大化发挥、完美执行，看看我们最终能落到什么位置。"
Slater 本周末将全力以赴争取带着 F3 冠军离开，但 奥迪 和他的管理团队将开始权衡他 2027 年的选择。
detailEn: As Formula 1 debuts in Madrid, Audi's first F1 protege will be vying to maintain his 100% title-winning streak on the undercard in the Formula 3 title-decider.

F3 championship leader Freddie Slater was the first-ever signing to Audi's F1 driver development programme at the start of 2026, a major coup for the German manufacturer, given he's been courted by F1 teams ever since his silverware-filled start in karting.

Slater and his management team deliberately resisted pairing with an F1 team earlier in his career despite a litany of offers - similar to Max Verstappen and Lando Norris who waited until they were in F3 before accepting the support of Red Bull and McLaren respectively.
"There was a bit of attraction probably in karting, but at that time it wasn't right [to join an F1 team's programme]," Slater told The Race.
"Me and my management team, my family and the people around me, we knew it wasn't the right kind of point in my career because I didn't need it. It was about just developing through the ranks.
"But now, going to Formula 3, it was the perfect opportunity to kind of develop into more of an experienced driver and hopefully a future Formula 1 driver. Perfect timing now.
"It felt more like a family to me and that's what really attracted me to it. It didn't feel like I was going into a business.
"It felt like I was actually going to a family that kind of had a lot of trust in me and that's why I wouldn't choose anyone else."
The 18-year-old's track record since graduating from karting is right up there with the most impressive junior CVs on the F1 grid now.
He won 16 of the 20 races en route to winning the Ginetta Junior championship in 2023, followed by winning 15 of the 20 races in a title-winning Italian F4 campaign in 2024.
Slater then switched to the Formula Regional European Championship (an intermediate step between F3 and F4), winning eight of the 20 races, backing up all of that star quality he showed in karting.
It means he has a 100% title-winning record for his full-time programme since graduating from karting; he's only been beaten in short winter series or championships where he only raced part-time.

Slater heads into F3's Madrid finale as the championship leader, having been the standout driver this year despite being a rookie. He's been in a league of his own in terms of average qualifying position.
He's also finished on the podium in six of the eight feature races this year, and he was only denied in Monza because of a mechanical failure.

Without that failure, Trident driver Slater was set to head into Madrid with a comfortable lead. Instead, he has a slender 15-point buffer over his only realistic title rival, ex-McLaren junior Ugo Ugochukwu, with 67 points up for grabs in Madrid.
"Previous success definitely gives you confidence and kind of people expect a lot of things, but I think F3 is a very interesting season," Slater said.
"Lots of things happen, and also I'm battling a lot of second-year drivers [such as Ugochukwu], who are also very good.
"So it was never going to be a walk in the park. I've had to kind of catch up on a lot of experience and get on the pace very quickly.
"As you saw in the second half of the season, I've kind of settled into a nice rhythm, obviously getting to know the car more.
"Now we're fighting for a championship, and it was nearly kind of job done [on Sunday in Monza], which is a bit unfortunate, but now we've full focus on Madrid."
Slater says he learned "not trying to go for too much" when "a lot of the things are out of your control sometimes in this championship".
He learned it was sensible to "pick up a fourth from the fifth where it was necessary and not trying to make too much out of the race and try and be a hero".
"I've matured a lot as a driver, letting the race come towards me more instead of trying to force a situation.
"That's definitely been one of the key factors that puts [you] in a position to win the championship."

Slater hasn't really had an off weekend this season, having never qualified outside the top 10 all season. Barcelona comes closest as he qualified 10th there and ended up eighth in the feature race - but he was still second in the sprint race there.
But after that weekend, Slater had an important reset that allowed him to kick on and build a championship lead.
"After Monaco and Barcelona, we all had a big kind of reset of me and the team coming together," Slater said.

"The team gave me a car that kind of suits me more. I've adapted my driving style to the F3 car more as I've gained more experience. I think it's just a combination of things throughout the season that's kind of picked up the momentum."
That certainly worked for Slater, who has scored 55 points in the last four rounds (despite the Monza DNF and a collision with Ugochukwu at Spa) compared to the 22 scored by nearest rival Ugochukwu.
Given there were 19 red flags across two days of F3's test there, the Madrid finale could be chaos.
Slater said of Madrid: "I loved it. I thought the track was incredible. I think it had character. It was a bit more old school.

"All these new tracks that are coming out, they're smooth, they're flat, it doesn't feel as exciting to drive them. Madrid reminds me of Macau and Monaco, those sort of tracks, Oulton Park in the UK, where you actually have a bit of excitement, bumps, and walls actually closing in on you.
"It's a lot more fun to drive. I can't wait to get out there for the qualifying run on Friday, which is going to be probably one of the most exciting parts of the weekend."
But will Slater be driving with the points situation in the back of his mind?
"No, no, it's been the same thought all year. It's execution - just maximise the results," Slater said.
"[At Monza], we maximised every ounce of the result we could have. Things have gone wrong out of our control and that's motorsport at the end of the day.
"Hopefully we can have some better luck because this year there's been quite a few things that have gone wrong that actually haven't been in my control that put us in bad situations.
"But I think in terms of myself and the way I've been driving, I couldn't be driving at a higher level and I'm definitely proving that.
"So I can't wait for Madrid and now it's just maximise, execute and see where we end up."
Slater's fully focused on walking away with the F3 title this weekend, but Audi and his management team will be weighing up his options for 2027.

detailZh: F1西班牙大奖赛值得关注的五件事
本周末西班牙大奖赛将迎来新的举办地
本周末，一级方程式将迎来西班牙大奖赛的新主办地，马德里环赛道将在西班牙首都郊区首次亮相。
它将取代此前举办西班牙大奖赛的巴塞罗那，后者仍在F1赛历上，但已更名为新名称，并已于6月举办了其2026年的比赛——由刘易斯·汉密尔顿夺冠。
本周末将是马德里自1981年老牌哈拉马赛道以来首次出现在F1赛历上，这也是大奖赛期间众多热议话题之一。
以下是值得关注的五件事。
任何新赛事都需要一定的磨合期。以第一届迈阿密大奖赛为例，餐饮设施位置欠佳，导致难以为贵宾区提供热食。
哦不！难道没有人会心疼那些可怜的VIP和他们变冷的开胃小点吗？
要知道，蒙扎举办大奖赛的历史远早于世界锦标赛的创办，而进出赛道至今仍是一场纯粹混乱的考验。阿布扎比也是如此，自2009年起每年举办F1，访客们却常常纳闷，为何大门口的安排依然一团糟。
因此，当我们的赛道团队抵达马德里赛道时（好吧，也许Fil除外，他仍被困在巴塞罗那与马德里之间的某趟火车上），找不到任何从媒体中心到围场的路，也就不足为奇了。同样被发现四处游荡、一脸茫然（两头茫然）的还有Pedro de la Rosa和安东内利。
后勤混乱将加剧车队搭建设备时面临的挑战，尤其这是背靠背赛事的第二站。假设车手们能找到他们的车库，而且那里有车可开，谁又能预料一旦赛车上道会出现什么样的乱子呢？
新铺设的沥青往往会出现问题，不过据说路面已经过高压清洗以去除油性残留物。而且，在一大堆线路最近被盗之后，我们只能希望所有的标识牌还能正常运作……
上周末的意大利大奖赛，或许是乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）首次公开承认他的总冠军希望实际上已经破灭。这位梅赛德斯车手在蒙扎获得亚军，负于队友基米·安东内利（安东内利），这意味着这位20岁的意大利车手目前在剩下10轮比赛的情况下已建立起66分的领先优势。
“是啊，基米确实掌控着局面，而且他有资格掌控局面，”他说。“我甚至都没有去想什么争夺或者反击之类的事情。我只是专注于一场一场比赛地对待，努力在每个周末都做到最好。”
“他的表现极其出色。要弥补这个差距将非常困难，所以我基本上就是接受现实吧。从现在开始我只想享受比赛，并尽可能多地赢下比赛。”
这肯定不是拉塞尔所预想的2026年赛季走向。赛季开始时，他是众望所归的夺冠大热门，并在墨尔本揭幕战中从杆位发车并夺冠，印证了这一标签。然而随后几轮比赛中运气并没有站在他这边，比如日本的时机不巧的安全车。但蒙扎一役恰恰证明了安东内利为什么是当之无愧的领跑者——要知道，他可是从第19位发车的！
如果拉塞尔（Russell）在那样一个周末都无法占据优势——那个周末他二年级队友还带着罚退发车——那么很难看出他还能在哪里占据上风并实现翻盘。
所以本周末的马德里大奖赛只是安东内利（Antonelli）加冕之路上又一场比赛——而且不要赌他在2026年拿不到第八场胜利！
角田裕毅（Tsunoda）本为一次性回归，如今已变成三场比赛
不久之前，多家F1媒体——包括本媒体在内——还把角田裕毅在赞德沃特的回归称为“一次性出场”。然而，现在这位日本车手即将为小红牛车队进行他今年第三次大奖赛正赛发车，同样地，劳森（劳森）也将继续为红牛车队出战。
这是由于红牛常规车手伊萨克·哈贾尔（哈贾尔）仍在与八月夏休期间在健身房训练中受伤的手腕伤势作斗争，他先缺席了赞德福特站，随后又缺席了蒙扎站，而马德里站将使他连续缺席第三场比赛。
虽然这对哈贾尔来说显然令人失望，但对于劳森和角田裕毅来说，这却是一个绝佳的机会，因为两人2026年的计划都尚未确定。对劳森而言，他或许应该对自己的未来最为放松，因为这位新西兰车手今年在小红牛的表现确实令人印象深刻，稳定地获得积分，并在过去两轮为红牛出战时表现英勇。
与此同时，角田裕毅尚未获得2026年的全职席位，据了解他正在洽谈明年参加IndyCar的比赛。因此他不太可能获得2027年的F1席位，但他并没有放弃全部希望，马德里站只是他展示自己真正实力的又一次机会——去年在红牛的艰难经历损害了他大部分声誉。
这位日本车手在赞德福特表现稳健，随后在蒙扎拿到了一个积分，考虑到小红牛目前领跑中游集团，如果他再取得一个前十名的成绩，也不必过于惊讶。
上个月当F3前往马德里赛道进行官方测试时，一些车队老板和赞助商可能会感到困惑。最终结果是出现了19次红旗，其中包括多起重大撞车事故，推高了事故账单。
与任何新赛道一样，第一年的抓地力水平会极低。但马德里赛道由公共道路和缓冲区极少的定制高速路段混合而成，很可能导致一个混乱的周末。
很多注意力将集中在马德里赛道的标志性特点——坡度陡峭的La Monumental弯道上，它比乍看起来要复杂得多，具有变化的半径和海拔变化。
但在令人印象深刻的12号弯之前和之后的弯角也极其棘手，有很多出弯墙直接延伸回赛道而不是逐渐远离。由于有如此多的未知因素，这项赛事的首届比赛很有可能变得一团糟。
"我认为，考虑到他们设置的护栏和赛道的设计，这肯定会是近来一级方程式最大的挑战之一，"担任该赛事大使的塞恩斯说。
"这条赛道让我想起很多吉达，让我想起很多巴库，在某些方面甚至让我有点想起澳门。所以开着1000马力的F1赛车跑这样的赛道，将会是一个非常有趣的挑战。"
Sainz知道F3测试中发生的事情，他并不抱有幻想：马德里赛道可能会成为混乱的温床，无论是在排位赛中车手们在距离护墙仅几毫米处寻找极限，还是随时可能出现的阻挡事故的威胁。
"我一直在研究这条赛道，也听说了F3测试中发生的事情，"他补充道。"我想我们都在预期排位赛中会出现安全车、红旗和黄旗之类的情况。"
“最近一级方程式有前往这类赛道的趋势，比如吉达和巴库，它们更靠近市区，还有迈阿密，但这些赛道有更多的护墙，而我们没有遇到过任何问题。”,
在汉密尔顿发表“没有规则”的言论后，法拉利成为了焦点
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
继两位法拉利车手在蒙扎发生碰撞之后，本周末所有人的目光都将聚焦于在马德里的汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔，以及车队是否会回应这位英国车手对更明确车队规则的呼吁。
勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在周日发车时并排驶入一号弯的减速弯。这位七届世界冠军在1号弯选择了内线，但这位摩纳哥车手守住位置并在2号弯抢到内侧线路，没有给他的队友留下任何空间，队友被迫驶入砂石区，因此损失了多个名次，引发了愤怒。
汉密尔顿认为自己本应获得优先权，因为他在车手积分榜上比勒克莱尔更接近梅赛德斯两位车手，他还借此抨击法拉利，回忆起自己在梅赛德斯时期事情的运作方式，声称马拉内罗“没有任何规则”。
当F1前往陌生的马德里赛道赛道时，法拉利对该赛道已有一定了解，因为车队曾在7月在那里进行过一次拍摄日。这是否会带来优势还有待观察，但可以肯定的是：法拉利必须让两位车手之间达成更清晰的理解，才能前往西班牙大奖赛。
detailEn: Five things to look out for at the F1 Spanish GP
There will be a new host of the Spanish Grand Prix this weekend
Formula 1 will welcome a new host of the Spanish Grand Prix this weekend as the Madring will make its debut on the outskirts of Spain’s capital city.
It is replacing previous Spanish GP holder Barcelona, which is still on the F1 calendar but under a new name having hosted its 2026 race in June - won by Lewis Hamilton.
This weekend will be the first time Madrid has appeared on the F1 calendar since the old-school Jarama circuit in 1981 and is one of many things that will be a talking point during the grand prix.
So here are five things to look out for.

With any new event there’s a certain amount of bedding in. Take the first iteration of the Miami Grand Prix, where the sub-optimal location of the catering facilities led to difficulties supplying hot food to the hospitality enclosures.
Oh no! Will nobody think of the poor VIPs and their cold canapes?

Mind you, Monza has been hosting grands prix since long before the world championship began and simply getting in and out of the track remains an essay in pure chaos. Ditto Abu Dhabi, where visitors often have cause to ponder why the arrangements at the gate remain a fustercluck when they’ve been hosting F1 annually since 2009.

To that end it was no surprise when our track team arrived at the Madring (well, maybe not Fil, still trapped on a train somewhere between Barcelona and Madrid) and couldn’t find any way to get from the media centre to the paddock. Also spotted wandering around looking lost: Pedro de la Rosa and Kimi Antonelli.

Logistical disarray will add to the challenges facing the teams setting up their equipment, given that this is the second race of a double-header. Assuming the drivers can find their way to their garages, and that there are cars there to drive, who knows what manner of malarkey could ensue once the cars hit the track?

Recently laid asphalt has a habit of misbehaving, although apparently the surface has been pressure-washed to get rid of the oily residues. And let’s hope all the signage still works, after a whole bunch of wiring was stolen recently…

Last weekend’s Italian Grand Prix was perhaps the first time George Russell publicly acknowledged that his title hopes were practically over. The Mercedes driver finished runner-up to team-mate Kimi Antonelli at Monza, meaning the 20-year-old Italian has now established a 66-point lead with 10 rounds remaining.

"Yeah, Kimi's definitely in control of it and he's deserving to be in control of it," he said. "I'm not even thinking about a fight or a comeback or anything. I'm just focused on taking it race by race and trying to maximise every single weekend.

"He's performing incredibly well. It's going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap, so I'm just sort of accepting that is what it is. I'm just going to enjoy it from here on in and try and win as many races as possible."

This is certainly not how Russell thought 2026 would pan out, entering the season as the heavy title favourite and supporting that tag by winning the Melbourne opener from pole. Luck subsequently didn’t go his way in the following rounds, such as the untimely safety car in Japan, but Monza was demonstrative of how Antonelli is the deserving leader – considering he started the race in 19th!
If Russell can’t even take advantage on a weekend like that, where his sophomore team-mate was carrying a grid penalty, then it’s hard to see where he will hold the upper hand and perform a comeback.
So Madrid this weekend is just another race on the path to Antonelli’s crowning moment – and don’t bet against him taking an eighth victory of 2026!
The one-off Tsunoda return that has turned into three races

It wasn’t long ago that several F1 media outlets – this one included – were labelling Yuki Tsunoda’s return at Zandvoort as a ‘one-off appearance’. Yet, here we are, with the Japanese driver set to make his third grand prix start of the year for Racing Bulls, likewise for Liam Lawson at Red Bull.

This comes as the result of usual Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar still battling with a wrist injury that he sustained during a gym session over the August summer break, first missing Zandvoort and then Monza, with Madrid set to make it three in a row.

While it obviously comes as a disappointment for Hadjar, it has presented a golden opportunity for both Lawson and Tsunoda with neither of their plans for 2026 yet confirmed. For Lawson, he should probably be the most relaxed over his future as the Kiwi has certainly impressed for Racing Bulls this year by scoring consistent points finishes and performing valiantly in the past two rounds for Red Bull.

Tsunoda, meanwhile, has been without a full-time seat in 2026 and is understood to be in talks for an IndyCar drive next year. So a spot on the F1 grid in 2027 is unlikely, but he hasn’t given up all hope and Madrid is just another chance for him to show what he can actually do after his torrid Red Bull stint last year damaged much of his reputation.

The Japanese driver performed solidly in Zandvoort before scoring a point in Monza, and considering Racing Bulls is leading the midfield, one shouldn’t be too shocked if he were to claim another top 10 result.

When F3 headed to the Madring for an official test last month, some team owners and sponsors will have likely scratched their heads. The end result was 19 red flags, including a number of significant crashes that drove up the accident bills.

As is always the case with any new circuit, the grip levels will be extremely low in year one. But Madring's hybrid of public roads and bespoke high-speed sections with little runoff area could well lead to a chaotic weekend.
A lot of attention will go to the Madring's headline feature, the steeply banked La Monumental curve and is a lot more complex than it first seems, with its varying radii and elevation changes.

But the corners right before and after the impressive Turn 12 are also extremely tricky, with plenty of exit walls that come back into the track rather than fade away. With so many unknowns, there is every chance the first running of the event could become a messy one.

"I think definitely with the way they've put the barriers and the design of the track, it's going to be one of the biggest challenges in Formula 1 recently," said Carlos Sainz, who is an ambassador for the event.

"The track reminds me a lot of Jeddah, reminds me a lot of Baku, even reminds me a bit of Macau in some ways. So having that in an F1 car with 1,000 horsepower is going to be quite an interesting challenge."

Sainz was aware of what happened in the F3 test and was under no illusion that the Madring could be a recipe for chaos, both in qualifying with drivers searching for the limit millimetres away from the walls, and the omnipresent threat of impeding incidents.
"I've been looking at the track and hearing of what happened in the F3 test,” he added. “I think we are all expecting safety cars and red flags and yellow flags in qualifying and things like this.
“It's been a tendency of Formula 1 to go to these kinds of tracks like Jeddah and Baku recently, that are closer to the city, Miami, but they have more walls and we haven't had any issues with it."
Ferrari is under the spotlight after Hamilton’s “there are no rules” remarks
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

Eyes will be on Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Madrid this weekend following the clash between the two Ferrari drivers at Monza, and on whether the team will respond to the Briton’s calls for clearer team rules.

Leclerc and Hamilton went side by side into the opening chicane at the start on Sunday. The seven-time world champion went for the inside at Turn 1, but the Monegasque held on and took the inside line for Turn 2, leaving no room for his team-mate, who was forced into the gravel and consequently lost several positions, causing anger.

Hamilton felt he should have been given priority, as he is closer to the Mercedes duo than Leclerc in the drivers’ championship, and took a swipe at Ferrari by recalling how things worked during his time at Mercedes, claiming that “there are no rules” at Maranello.

While F1 heads into unknown territory at the Madring, Ferrari already has some knowledge of the venue from a filming day the team conducted there in July. Whether that will give it an advantage remains to be seen, but one thing is certain: Ferrari must arrive at the Spanish Grand Prix with a clearer understanding between its two drivers.
